_comment: Personal missions (issue #113, scripts/personal_missions.gd + scripts/mission_script.gd). At bond rank 4 each core character's story becomes a short hand-built mission on the Command Table; rank 5 needs it done. who: recruit id (field heroes are forced into the party; core staff come along as an escort the party keeps alive, escort_hp). province: where the Command Table offers it. map: a set-piece map from tools/make_personal.py whose @spot lines the steps point at. brief, threat (1-5), enemies (spawn weights shown as 'Expect'), rewards (paid on success), standing (faction changes on success), xp, label (the HUD line before the first step). steps: see scripts/mission_script.gd (talk, goto, clear, hold, use, exit; banter, say, creep, done_say, done_banter, label). speakers and talks merge into Dialogue.data() like data/story.json; every speaker needs a portrait in assets/portraits/.

personal_bran_intro.title: Buy Back the Paper
lines: Gallows Ferry at low water. The river smells of tar and other people's money. A counting-house squats on the landing with its shutters half open, like a man pretending to be asleep.
bran
That's 'im. Ozias Crane. Buys contracts by the barrel, sells 'em by the pound. Mine's been passed round more than the collection plate.
bran
His nephews'll be about. Big lads. Not bright. They 'it like debt collectors 'cause that's what they are.
bran
I got the money. Every coin I never spent on you. If he takes it, nobody gets hurt. If 'e don't...
He rolls his shoulders. The tattoo on his forearm creaks like a tightened belt.
bran
Then clause nine's about to get a workout.

personal_bran_broker.title: Crane & Nephews
lines: Inside, the counting-house is all ledgers and lamp smoke. Ozias Crane sits behind a desk the size of a coffin, pen already wet.
crane
Brannoc Tolley. I wondered when you'd come in out of the rain. And you've brought... something. It doesn't appear to be anyone.
bran
Me paper, Crane. I'm buying it back. Full price. Then you strike your name off my arm, in your own hand, while I watch.
crane
Full price? Brannoc. A contract like yours appreciates. The more people you've hit for me, the more you're worth to whoever holds you.
bran
Name a number.
crane
I'd rather name a buyer. The Guild has been asking after you. They're downstairs. They're early, actually. I may have mentioned you'd be calling.
smug
Boots on the stairs outside. A lot of them.
bran
Right. Ash, keep 'em off the door. I'm gonna stand here and watch him write very slowly.
crane
You can't seriously expect me to... 'ere, put that down...
bran
Pen. Paper. Arm. Start writing.
angry

personal_bran_outro.title: Clause Nine
lines: The last Guild sellsword limps down the landing. Inside, Crane has struck his own name from Bran's arm, line by line, his hand shaking hard enough to blot every stroke.
crane
There. Satisfied? You're held by nobody. A contract with no holder. It isn't even legal. It's just... ink.
bran
And this is your money. All of it. I said I'd pay, and I pay.
Bran drops the purse on the desk. Then he takes Crane's pen, looks at it for a long moment, and walks out onto the landing.
There is a small splash.
bran
Don't look at me like that. It was a terrible pen.
smug
bran
Come on. Let's go 'ome before I start feelin' things.

personal_gristle_intro.title: Collect from Hester Vane
lines: The Gutterwoods close over the path like a hand. Letters hang from the branches in their thousands, sealed, addressed, never sent.
gristle
Coven ground starts at the totems. Past them, every tree is a witness, and every witness talks.
gristle
Hester will know we're here before we do. Moths first, she'll send. Then the nephews. Then she'll come out herself, wearing her sad face.
gristle
Eleven years, dear. Eleven years of interest on one life. Kept the receipt, I have.
She pats a fold of her shawl. Something in it crackles, old and much-folded.

personal_gristle_tree.title: The Coven Tree
lines: The Coven tree is older than the woods around it. Every name carved in its bark is a witch, living or dead. There is a smooth, pale scar where one name used to be.
hester
Gristle. Always did know how to make an entrance, you did. Usually through someone else's front door.
gristle
Hester. Terrible, you look. I'd charge you for the diagnosis, but you owe me enough already.
hester
I owe you a grandson. I know. Thought of it every day for eleven years, I have.
gristle
Then you've had plenty of time to find a knife, haven't you. Put my name back, Hester. Where it was. Deep.
hester
The tree decides, not me. It wants to know you're still one of us. It will test you. The woods will come for the tree, and you will defend it, or you won't.
gristle
Ugh. Ceremony. Fine. Ash, dear, hit anything that tries to eat the tree. Anything. The Coven gets the bill.
smug

personal_gristle_outro.title: Paid in Full
lines: The last moth falls in a flutter of torn envelopes. The woods go quiet, the way a room goes quiet after an argument.
hester
It's done. Satisfied, the tree is. I am... not sure I am, but the tree is.
Hester takes a little curved knife from her sleeve and carves, slowly and deep, into the pale scar: GRISTLE.
hester
Grown, he has, you know. My grandson. Children of his own. They have your fever-tonic recipe pinned in the kitchen.
gristle
Then they owe me too. I'll send a bill.
But she doesn't. She stands looking at her name in the bark for a long time, and when Hester cries, Gristle hands her a handkerchief and only charges her half.

personal_ninefingers_intro.title: Find Hob's Wick
lines: The Tithe Road runs straight and grey toward the capital. Every mile there is a Concord noticeboard. Every noticeboard has a face on it.
ninefingers
That's me. WANTED: CORPORAL DARO, DESERTER. Gave me a bigger chin. Flattered and offended.
ninefingers
Hob's Wick's off the road, two miles past the toll post. If it's still there.
ninefingers
Tear the posters down as we go. Not vanity. Every toll man on this road's looked at that face twenty times a day. Rather they forgot it.
They pull their hood lower. It does not help with the chin.

personal_ninefingers_village.title: Smoke from the Mill
lines: Over the rise: a mill wheel turning, a chapel roof, goats where goats should not be. Hob's Wick. Every house still standing.
ninefingers
It's there. It's all... there.
But the fields to the east have gone pale at the edges, and something is crawling out of the white toward the nearest house.
ninefingers
No. Not after all this. Didn't lose a finger keeping this place on the map to watch it get bloody nibbled.
angry
ninefingers
Ash. Hold the line at the village. Nothing gets past the well.

personal_ninefingers_outro.title: Roll of Honour
lines: Inside the chapel it is cool and smells of candle wax. The villagers have followed you in, at a respectful distance, to see who drove off the white.
On the wall by the altar there is a small brass plaque. Daro reads it twice.
CORPORAL DARO. FALLEN AGAINST THE BLANK. SHE KEPT US ON THE MAP.
ninefingers
Got the pronoun wrong. And the dying. And the bit about the Blank. Concord told them I died a hero so nobody has to say I ran.
sad
An old woman touches Daro's sleeve and asks, very politely, if they knew the Corporal.
ninefingers
Yeah. Knew them. Bit of a mouth on them. They'd have liked it here.
ninefingers
Come on, Ash. Let's go before some civvy offers me a drink and I have to explain the finger.

personal_quill_intro.title: Correct the Original
lines: Old Mill Crossing. The mill still turns, slow and creaking. Across the millrace, behind a Concord barricade, sits an iron strongbox on a seized cart.
quill
There. Records of the Hollowmark Office. My handwriting on every page. Thirty-one people written off, alphabetically.
quill
I'll need it open, and then I'll need time. Correcting a Concord ledger isn't striking a line through. It has to look as though it was always right.
quill
I don't fight. I want that duly minuted. I once lost an argument with a goose. Stay close to me.
Quill clutches a pen case to their chest like a holy relic. It is, in a way.

personal_quill_open.title: Thirty-one Lines
lines: The strongbox groans open. Inside: one fat ledger, bound in Concord grey, and a smell of old ink and older guilt.
quill
Hello, you. It's been a long time.
quill
Abernathy, Celia. Written off, unproductive. Bell, Tomas. Written off, unproductive. Bell, Tomas the younger...
Quill's voice catches. Then they sit down in the dust with the ledger on their knees and uncap the good pen.
quill
Give me time. And please, please don't let anything eat me while I'm concentrating.

personal_quill_outro.title: Carried Forward
lines: Quill blots the last line and holds the ledger up to the light. Thirty-one entries that said WRITTEN OFF now say CARRIED FORWARD, in a hand nobody alive could tell from the original.
quill
There. Per the record, they never stopped counting. The Ledger can see them again.
quill
It won't bring anyone back from wherever the Blank put them. I know that. But if it ever lets anyone go, they'll have somewhere to come home to. On paper, at least.
They put the ledger back in the strongbox and close the lid gently, like a coffin, or a cradle.
quill
Let's go. And thank you, Ash. I'll write you a receipt. A real one.

personal_tobble_intro.title: Fetch the Last Drop's Sign
lines: The Frayed Meadow, far side. The grass grows in half-sentences here, and then in single words, and then not at all.
tobble
Over the ridge. You'll see it. What's left. Thirty year I pulled pints there, and now the Blank drinks for free.
tobble
The sign hangs over the door. A mug, a crack, THE LAST DROP in gold. I'll get it down. Ladder's my job. Hitting things is yours.
tobble
And go easy. My knees aren't what they were. They weren't much then, neither.

personal_tobble_ruin.title: The Last Drop
lines: The Last Drop is a shell. The roof is gone, the windows are gone, and a step from the door the ground stops being ground and starts being white.
The sign still hangs from its iron bracket, swinging a little. Old gold letters, peeling: THE LAST DROP.
tobble
There she is. Hello, old girl.
tobble
Right. Ladder up. Give us a minute with the bracket. It's rusted on, like everything else I own.
The white shifts. It has noticed you. Things begin to climb out of it.

personal_tobble_outro.title: Last Orders
lines: Back on the ridge, out of breath. Tobble sits on a stump with the sign across his knees, picking a flake of white from the corner of the mug.
tobble
Got her. Got her, and the doorstep went a minute after. A minute! I've cut it finer at closing time, mind.
tobble
Look at that crack. That's from the night Bran's old captain tried to arm-wrestle a Concord magistrate. Lost. Sign fell on him. Best night of the year, that were.
He laughs until he has to wipe his eyes, and blames it on the dust.
tobble
Home, then. I know just where she's going.

personal_abeyance_intro.title: Follow the Page
lines: The Wickham Hills. Ink wells up between the stones and runs downhill in black threads, toward a valley nobody marked on any map.
abeyance
The page has drawn the way. Look: the hills, the road, three little marks, and an X. It's never drawn anything before. It usually just complains about my spelling.
abeyance
I'll read the way, you keep things off me. I'm told I'm a terrible fighter. I've never tried, so I can't in conscience argue.
She holds the page up to the light. The lines on it move, very slightly, like something breathing.

personal_abeyance_door.title: Not Today
lines: The chapel stands where the page said, small and grey, and you are fairly sure it was not there a moment ago. The door is shut. There is no handle.
abeyance
Hello? I've brought something of yours. I think. Or you've brought something of mine.
From behind the door, a voice. Very polite. Very tired.
"Not today."
abeyance
Oh, I know that one. That's what the Abbot used to say. It means 'ask nicely and keep asking'.
abeyance
I'll read to it. The whole page, aloud, as many times as it takes. Like Compline. Don't let anything interrupt me. Doors hate being interrupted.

personal_abeyance_outro.title: The Missing Page
lines: Mid-sentence, the door swings open on its own. Inside: dust, a lectern, and a book with every page in place but one.
Hild walks in very slowly. The page in her hands goes still for the first time since she stole it.
abeyance
You fit. Of course you fit. You were never mine, were you.
She lays the page in the gap. The book closes by itself. When it opens again, there is one new line on the page, and she copies it into her notebook without letting you see.
abeyance
Let's go home. I'll tell you what it said when we get there. I need to pray on what it means first.

personal_ottoline_intro.title: Answer the Knocking
lines: Gallows Ferry, the east bank. Lantern Row used to be the brightest street on the river. Now half of it is white, and the lamps along what's left burn for nobody.
ottoline
Encore were at the end. Red door, brass handle. I stood outside it every night for nine year with my arms folded.
ottoline
Six year ago I stood outside it with my back against it, and I didn't let anyone out.
Somewhere ahead, from inside the white, comes a sound. Knock. Knock. Knock. Knock. Knock. Knock. Then a wait.
ottoline
Six. Always six. Come on. And whatever comes out of that white, it doesn't touch me before I get to that door.
angry

personal_ottoline_door.title: Six Knocks
lines: The door stands in the white with no building round it. Red paint, brass handle, Ottoline's chalk tally marks still on the frame: one for every night she kept it.
Knock. Knock. Knock. Knock. Knock. Knock.
ottoline
I hear you.
She raises one enormous fist and knocks back. Six times. Slow.
The white around the door begins to stir, like a crowd getting to its feet.
ottoline
Keep it off the door. Give us a minute. I've waited six year. I can wait one more minute, but it can't have this door.
sad

personal_ottoline_outro.title: Coat Check
lines: Ottoline turns the brass handle and opens the door. Behind it there is no stage, no bar, no people. Just the cloakroom: a counter, and six coats on six hooks.
ottoline
Oh.
She takes them down one at a time and folds each over her arm, as carefully as if someone were still inside it.
ottoline
There. They hand you a ticket. You give them their coat back. They go home.
Behind you, very faintly, one knock. Ottoline doesn't turn round. She just nods, once, and carries the coats out of the white.

personal_jessamy_intro.title: Back on the Books
lines: The Tithe Road after dark. Lamps at every toll post, and between them the kind of dark that has a smell. Jessamy is easier to see at night. She says that's the point.
jessamy
Toll Post Nine. Notary Fennick keeps late hours. Strikin' people out pays better after supper.
jessamy
He's got friends with crossbows, and the friends have friends. We go up the back lane, quiet, and knock at his window. He'll adore that.
smug
jessamy
And Ash? If I start goin' see-through in the lamplight, ignore it. It's a skin condition. It's called the Concord.

personal_jessamy_marrow.title: The Notary
lines: A rap at the shutter. A rattle of the latch. Notary Fennick opens his window and finds Jessamy's face an inch from his own.
marrow
You. You're... I struck you out. You paid me to, duly. I remember the fee. It was a very good fee.
jessamy
And now I'd like a refund, Fennick. In ink. Write me back in.
marrow
That's not how it works. Once you're out of the Ledger you're out. Per the statute. That's the whole point of being out.
jessamy
Then make it how it works. You're a notary. Notarise something.
angry
Outside, someone shouts. A lantern swings toward the toll house. Then another.
marrow
The clerks! They'll see you! They'll see me! They'll audit me!
jessamy
Then you'd better write fast. Ash, cully, keep 'em off the house. Fennick and I have paperwork.

personal_jessamy_outro.title: Occupation: Yes
lines: It takes Fennick an hour. His hand shakes so badly he ruins three sheets. Jessamy stands at his shoulder and reads every word.
marrow
Name. Jessamy Leake. Residence... Hollowmark, apparently, God help it. Occupation?
jessamy
Put 'yes'.
marrow
That isn't an occupation.
jessamy
It is now. Seal it.
smug
The seal comes down. Jessamy holds her hand up to the lamp. For the first time in years, the light does not go through it.
jessamy
Oh. Oh, that's... I'd forgotten I had knuckles. Look at 'em. Horrible little things. I love them.

personal_odile_intro.title: Settle the Account
lines: Old Mill Crossing in the afternoon. Across the scarecrow fields stands an inn called the Honest Measure, which Odile says is the only honest thing for ten miles.
odile
She will be in the back room. Window seat. Two pens, one red, one black. She will have ordered tea and not drunk it.
odile
Something has been stitching the scarecrows back together out here. We go through them. Politely, if possible. Firmly, if not.
odile
And Ash. Whatever she says to me, do not look at me while she says it. I would rather you did not see my face.

personal_odile_meet.title: Red, Then Black
lines: The back room. Window seat. Two pens. Tea, untouched. Chief Assessor Marguerite Penhallow looks up from a ledger and does not smile.
penhallow
Odile. You are thinner. And you have brought a guard. Is it a guard? It does not appear on any register I know.
odile
It is Ash. Ash is not on any register, Mother. That is rather the point of Ash.
penhallow
I came to discuss the return of Concord property. The Lowmere ledger. And your post, which remains open. Nobody need ever know.
odile
I am not here to give anything back. I am here to audit you.
penhallow
Audit. Me.
odile
Forty years of perfect books. Let us see them.
angry
Outside the window, the scarecrows in the far field lurch upright, one after another, and turn toward the inn. Beyond them, the edge of the field has gone white.
penhallow
This will take some time. Hold the door, would you, whatever you are.

personal_odile_outro.title: Ninety Gilt
lines: Three hours, by the inn clock. When the last scarecrow falls, Odile is still at the window seat, the back of a menu covered edge to edge in figures.
odile
Every account balances. Every one. All but a single line, twenty-six years old. Ninety Gilt, quietly moved, so one village never made it onto the lists.
penhallow
Penhallow Mere.
odile
Where I was born.
For a long moment neither of them says anything. Then the Chief Assessor caps her red pen, and her black one, and stands.
penhallow
Keep the ledger, Odile. Use it better than I did.
sad
She pays for the tea, and the menu, and leaves. Odile does not cry until she is sure her mother is out of sight. Ash does not look.

personal_velvette_intro.title: The Last Performance
lines: Saltreed Marsh at dusk. Music carries over the reeds, brass and strings and laughter, from a painted showboat moored at the end of a long dock: the Gilded Heron.
velvette
Augustin always did love a full house. Tonight, he gets one.
velvette
His deckhands will be on the gangway, his bravos by the stage, and Augustin in his cabin counting tonight's takings. The commissions are in there with him.
velvette
I go on during the closing act. In costume, naturellement. You are my supporting cast. Try not to upstage me.
smug

personal_velvette_sallow.title: The Closing Act
lines: The closing act. A girl in white with a borrowed rapier faces a paying volunteer under the lamps. Fauvette walks out onto the stage between them, and the music stops.
sallow
Fauvette? Fauvette! Darling! Ma chérie! You're alive! Mesdames et messieurs, the star of the Crimson Encore! Applause!
velvette
Bonsoir, Augustin. I have come to give one last performance. One you did not book.
sallow
Now, now. We were all just following the commissions, weren't we? Papers. Signatures. Nobody ever made anyone do anything.
velvette
Eleven people, Augustin. You chose them. You counted the takings. And you put my name at the bottom of every page. 'The instrument'.
angry
sallow
Boys! The lady's had too much champagne. See her off the stage.
velvette
Oh good. An encore.

personal_velvette_outro.title: Eleven Names
lines: Fauvette steps back out onto the stage with the commission book open in one gloved hand. Augustin Sallow is on his knees by the footlights with her rapier resting, very lightly, on his shoulder.
velvette
Mesdames, messieurs. Tonight's closing act. A reading.
She reads the names. Eleven of them, slowly, with the price beside each. Nobody in the audience cheers. One by one, they take off their hats.
sallow
Please. Fauvette. Darling. Je vous en prie. What do you want?
velvette
Nothing, Augustin. You keep this book pinned to your coat until it reaches the Concord. Let us see how they reward a man who keeps receipts.
She closes the book and bows. It is the best bow you have ever seen.

missions.name: Buy Back the Paper
missions.brief: Bran's contract is held by Ozias Crane, a broker who keeps a counting-house on the Gallows Ferry landing. Bran wants to buy himself back, and wants Crane to strike his own name off the tattoo while he watches. Crane has nephews, and friends in the Guild.
missions.label: Find the counting-house

steps.label: Walk up the landing to Crane's counting-house
banter: bran
Tar, rope, river. Smells like me twenties.

steps.label: Get past Crane's nephews
banter: bran
Corrie! Still collectin' for your uncle? Still bad at it?

steps.label: Keep the Guild off the door while Crane writes
steps.fail: The Guild broke in. Crane slipped out the back with Bran's paper.

missions.name: Collect from Hester Vane
missions.brief: Coven elder Hester Vane owes Mother Gristle a life, and has for eleven years. Gristle is going to collect: not coin, but her name carved back on the Coven tree. The woods will have something to say about that.
missions.label: Find Coven ground

steps.label: Hester's moths come to look at you
banter: gristle
There they are. A love letter somebody never sent, every one of those is. Hit them anyway.

steps.label: Defend the Coven tree from the woods
steps.fail: The woods got to the tree first. Hester says the tree has decided. Gristle says the tree can bill her.

missions.name: Find Hob's Wick
missions.brief: The village Daro refused to strike out lies off the Tithe Road, past Concord toll posts with Daro's face on the posters. Daro needs to know whether it is still there. Even if it's white. Especially if it's white.
missions.label: Head down the Tithe Road

steps.label: Tear down Daro's wanted posters
banter: ninefingers
Twenty Gilt. Worth twenty Gilt. Been insulted by better bounties.

steps.label: Get through the toll post
banter: ninefingers
Abernathy. Trained me. He'll know the hood. Hit him before he knows the hood.

steps.label: Follow the mill smoke to Hob's Wick
Keep the white's crawlers out of Hob's Wick
steps.fail: The crawlers got into the houses. The villagers fled west, and Daro went quiet.

missions.name: Correct the Original
missions.brief: Quill's original ledger, with thirty-one people written off in Quill's own hand, sits in a Concord strongbox at Old Mill Crossing. Quill wants to correct it, and nobody else can forge Quill. Quill can't fight: get the strongbox open and keep them alive while they work.
missions.label: Get Quill to the strongbox

steps.label: Take Quill up the mill road
banter: quill
If anyone asks, I'm an auditor. Nobody attacks an auditor. Nobody wants to be near one.

steps.label: Keep everything off Quill while they correct the ledger

missions.name: Fetch the Last Drop's Sign
missions.brief: Tobble's old tavern in the Frayed Meadow is a roofless ruin at the Blank's edge, but its sign still hangs. He wants it back before the white does. Tobble can't fight and his knees are worse: keep the white and what climbs out of it off him while he works the bracket loose.
missions.label: Find the Last Drop

steps.label: Over the ridge toward the Last Drop
banter: tobble
Used to walk this every morning with a barrel on each shoulder. Now it's me as wants carrying.

steps.label: Hold the white back while Tobble gets the sign down
done_banter: Got her! Run! Well, tha run. I'll do summat near it.

steps.label: Run for it, before the white catches you

missions.name: Follow the Page
missions.brief: Sister Hild's stolen page drew a map: the Wickham Hills, a chapel nobody remembers, and an X. The page has never been this direct. Hild can't fight: follow the page's marks, keep her alive, and get her to the chapel.
missions.label: Follow the page

steps.label: Follow the page: the first mark
banter: abeyance
Left at the cairn that isn't there. Oh. There it is. It's shy.

steps.label: Follow the page: the second mark
banter: abeyance
The page says 'down the hill and mind the ink'. It's underlined 'mind'. Twice.

steps.label: Follow the page: the third mark
banter: abeyance
It's drawing faster now. I think it's excited. I think I am too.

steps.label: Keep everything off Hild while she reads to the door

missions.name: Answer the Knocking
missions.brief: On Gallows Ferry, where the white swallowed Lantern Row, the door of the Crimson Encore still stands, and something behind it knocks six times, then waits. Big Ottoline shut that door. She wants to be the one who opens it, and the white wants that door too.
missions.label: Walk down Lantern Row

steps.label: Walk down what's left of Lantern Row
banter: ottoline
That were the gin palace. That were the pawnbroker. That were Pell's mam's. She threw a lovely punch.

steps.label: Keep the white off the Encore's door
steps.fail: The white took the door. The knocking stopped. Ottoline stood at the edge until dark.

missions.name: Back on the Books
missions.brief: Notary Fennick struck Jessamy out of the Ledger for a fee, and she has been fading in daylight ever since. He still works Toll Post Nine on the Tithe Road, by night. A pen that takes you out can put you back in, if the hand holding it is frightened enough.
missions.label: Up the back lane

steps.label: Up the back lane to Toll Post Nine
banter: jessamy
Lamps Out works on clerks too. Mostly they just think they've had too much wine.

steps.label: Keep the clerks off the toll house while Fennick writes
steps.fail: The clerks broke in. Fennick fled through the back with his pen. Jessamy kept the inkwell.

steps.label: Back down the lane before dawn

missions.name: Settle the Account
missions.brief: Chief Assessor Marguerite Penhallow has written to her daughter: red ink, then black. She waits at the Honest Measure inn at Old Mill Crossing to discuss 'the return of Concord property'. Odile is going to settle up. Properly. Once. The scarecrows between here and there have other plans.
missions.label: Cross the fields to the inn

steps.label: Cross the scarecrow fields
banter: odile
Each of those scarecrows has a tithe tag on it. Someone has been taxing the crows.

steps.label: Hold the inn door while Odile audits her mother
steps.fail: The scarecrows broke in through the kitchen. The audit was never finished.

missions.name: The Last Performance
missions.brief: Augustin Sallow chose the Crimson Encore's 'volunteers' and counted the takings. Now he runs a showboat, the Gilded Heron, in the Saltreed Marsh, with the Office of Quiet's commissions in his cabin. Fauvette has one last performance to give, and his deckhands and bravos are the supporting cast.
missions.label: Board the Gilded Heron

steps.label: Walk out along the dock to the Gilded Heron
Sallow's deckhands
banter: velvette
Deckhands. Augustin always did hire by the pound.

steps.label: Take the commission book from Sallow's cabin
Leave the Heron to its audience
